rules.title: Massachusetts statewide rent control ballot question (struck from November 2026 ballot)
rules.requirement: Initiative petition that would have limited annual rent increases for residences, with exemptions for several types of units, including units operated solely for religious purposes. The Supreme Judicial Court ruled it cannot go on the November ballot because the religious exemption means it relates to religion, which the state Constitution bars from the ballot.

coverage.summary: Would have limited annual rent increases for residences statewide, with exemptions for several unit types including units operated solely for religious purposes; details not given in the article.

rules.exemptions: Several types of units, including ones operated solely for religious purposes, plus secular exemptions (not detailed).
rules.effective_date_note: Never took effect; struck from the 2026 ballot by the SJC (reported June 23, 2026). Proponents hinted at a 2028 petition.
rules.quoted_span: The state’s Supreme Judicial Court ruled a ballot question seeking to bring rent control back to Massachusetts cannot go forward this November, because it includes a religious exemption.
rules.review_note: Secondary news source; the petition number and the text of the measure are not given. Compromise legislation was urged but not passed per the article.

no_rule_findings.finding: Supreme Judicial Court ruling blocks the rent control ballot question from the November 2026 ballot. Proponents urged a compromise bill before July 1, but top lawmakers balked.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: In recent weeks, rent control supporters pushed for a compromise bill, urging state lawmakers to pass it as legislation before July 1.

result.doc_summary: WBUR article (June 23, 2026) reporting that the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court struck the statewide rent control ballot question from the November 2026 ballot because its exemption for religious-use units made it a petition relating to religion, which the state Constitution bars. Proponents may try again in 2028. A failed-measure record is captured for rent increase limits.
